gloss: to arrange; to discuss; to have a meeting

definitions.gloss: to have a meeting; to discuss
definitions.explanation: To meet and discuss plans, schedules, or details in advance.
To coordinate timing or actions with another person.

examples.japanese: イベントの{詳細|しょうさい}について{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせた。
examples.english: We had a meeting about the details of the event.

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}、クライアントと{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせがある。
examples.english: I have a meeting with the client tomorrow.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{事前|じぜん}に{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせていたようだ。
examples.english: It seems the two of them had arranged things beforehand.

notes:
{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせる is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) formed from {打|う}つ (to strike) + {合|あ}わせる (to match). Originally meaning to strike things together, it now means to coordinate or meet for discussion.

ASPECT (ている):
{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせている indicates a meeting is currently in progress.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [topic]について{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせる — to discuss [topic]
- [person]と{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせる — to have a meeting with [person]

NOUN FORM:
{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせ is the extremely common noun form meaning "meeting" or "briefing" in business contexts.
- {打|う}ち{合|あ}わせがある (have a meeting)
- {打|う}ち{合|あ}わせに{行|い}く (go to a meeting)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {事前|じぜん}に{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせる (arrange in advance)
- スケジュールを{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせる (coordinate schedules)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {会議|かいぎ}: formal meeting (larger, more structured)
- ミーティング: meeting (borrowed from English)
- {打|う}ち{合|あ}わせ: smaller, working-level discussion
